messages:
maya: FYI got an escalated repro from ACME — their rerank API is returning 422 / 'invalid input' for some documents, but only for certain user-generated strings with emojis + accents.
sam: any sample payload? can you paste the exact text that fails?
maya: here (redacted ids):
```
POST /v1/rerank\nContent-Type: application/json\n{\n  \"queries\": [\"search term\"],\n  \"candidates\": [\"I love this song 🎵\", \"Null\u0000byte here\", \"áé (a + combining)\" ]\n}\n```
maya: ACME says it only happens intermittently when their upstream system does some legacy escaping + they re-serialize JSON in Node.
jordan: interesting — that looks like two distinct problems: embedded NUL (U+0000) and grapheme clusters / ZWJ emoji sequences causing length/byte-count mismatch after normalization.
lee: @maya can you paste the API error lines from our logs? request-id would help.
maya: log snippet: `request_id=rc-8a3f2; rerank:400 -> body parse error: invalid utf8 sequence at offset 128`
Also: `client=acme-service; payload_bytes=984; parsed_utf8_bytes=980`
so it looks like a byte-length mismatch hitting our UTF-8 validation.
sam: do they use the official SDK or roll their own HTTP client?
maya: their stack: Node 14, custom fetch layer that does Buffer.from(str) at some point + they pass through strings from an older database that stores latin1 blobs.
jordan: likely repro path: latin1 bytes -> Buffer.from(string, 'latin1') -> toString() -> JSON.stringify -> server expects UTF-8 and validates length; combining sequences (like a + 0301) vs precomposed (á) can change normalized byte length too.
lee: short term workaround: sanitize on client: normalize to NFC and drop nulls: `s = s.normalize('NFC').replace(/\u0000/g, '')` then send. Also recommend `Buffer.from(s, 'utf8')` explicitly.
maya: ACME confirmed that removing NULs made the error go away in their load test. but they want a server-side fix because they can't guarantee all producers sanitize.
jordan: plan: 1) ingress sanitizer on rerank route — strip U+0000, run NFC normalization, and if bytes change unexpectedly return 400 with specific hint. 2) add telemetry to capture original vs normalized length and sample diffs (PII-scrubbed). 3) update SDK docs with best-practice snippet.
sam: any risk to changing normalization server-side (regression for customers relying on exact byte sequences)?
jordan: small risk. We'll gate behind a feature flag and rollout canary to internal + a few tolerant customers.
lee: created a quick patch PR for ingress sanitizer (internal link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rerank/ingress-sanitize/pull/42) — it strips U+0000 and runs NFC by default. Will add opt-out header `X-RW-Allow-raw-unicode: true` for strict apps.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rerank-ingress-sanitize PR #42 -> staging at 2024-10-18T13:40Z (pipeline green).
maya: I've told ACME the workaround and that we're rolling a canary. they've requested a repro script so they can validate post-fix.
sam: maya can you add the minimal curl/python repro to the thread for ACME? I can attach it to the support ticket.
maya: quick curl repro (replace TOKEN/IDs):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"queries":["q"],"candidates":["ok","Null\u0000here","man\u200dwoman\u200dchild\u200dbaby"]}'
```
maya: note: some emoji ZWJ sequences (man‍woman‍child‍baby) are valid UTF-8 but can be decomposed differently by some clients which causes the server's validator to see byte length mismatch.
jordan: followups: add e2e test that sends mixed-latin1/utf8 payloads, confirm server normalizes and returns either 200 or a clear 400 with remediation steps. also add a note in support runbook: when customer gets 422/400 mention: check for U+0000, run NFC, check client encoding.
sam: tagging @acme-ops in ticket; let's track until staging deploy is observed and ACME confirms.
maya: thanks folks — I'll update the ticket and paste ACME's confirmation once they validate on staging. :thumbsup:
